hook_text: Hand in, car up. Everything in between is a row of boxes, and one arrow along the bottom makes it a system.
clip_script: Any machine is a system: input, process, output. For the jack, input is your hand on the handle, oil in the store, the car. Process, in order: the lever makes your force ten times bigger; the pump pushes oil through a one-way valve, raising the pressure; pressurised oil enters the ram; the big ram turns pressure into a huge force and rises a few millimetres. Output: the car lifted and held, plus a little heat. Release is a branch back to the store. Now the loop: you watch the car and stop pumping, that is feedback and control. The overload valve does it automatically: sense pressure, compare with the rating, open and bypass. Brakes, water plants, recycling lines, all drawn the same way. A map of what happens, not a picture of parts.
visual_style: Whiteboard row of labelled boxes with arrows; force arrows growing and distance arrows shrinking between them; a feedback arrow curving back along the bottom; a side branch for release.
mood: Tidy, systematic, lightbulb at the loop.
pacing: Three stages, the jack's boxes in order, release branch, feedback loop, uses.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the systems diagram of a bicycle pump.
